title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 92
paragraphs: Thus he spoke, and to his words he added the deed; for at once the Samians gave assurance and sworn pledges of alliance with the Greeks, and having done so, the others sailed away home. Hegesistratos, however, he bade sail with the Greeks, considering his name a good omen for success. The Greeks then, after staying still that day, offered sacrifices for success on the next day, their diviner being Deïphonos son of Euenios, an Apolloniate — from that Apollonia which lies on the Ionian gulf.
